prize_parts.citation: for the theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and the Z2 topological insulator phase, and for its first experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: B028 alone, with Kane, Mele and Molenkamp. Round 1 sharpened the case in two ways. First, four members independently name the same trio, which matters because the credit boundary is the main objection and nobody has proposed a better three-person slate. Second, the chair asks what this prize says that 2016 did not. My answer is that the 2016 citation concerned topological phase transitions and topological invariants in model systems, with a magnetic field breaking time reversal in the quantum Hall case. Kane and Mele showed that spin-orbit coupling alone, with time-reversal symmetry intact, yields a Z2 invariant and protected helical edge states, a new class of matter that no one had to build a field around. Molenkamp's HgTe measurement then showed it in a device. I would write the citation around exactly that: the Z2 phase and its first observation. This keeps the statement inside what the trio can claim without dispute, and avoids a claim about all topological insulators that Hasan and the 3D theorists could rightly contest. The mechanism is simple and general, the experiment is quantitative, and about two decades of independent confirmation make the interpretation stable. The pairing mechanism in twisted graphene is still open, and the closed-form understanding of topological bands is the reason I rate B028 as the more mature case.
statement.case_against: The credit gap is not removed by a narrow citation. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang made the HgTe prediction that Molenkamp's group tested, and they are outside the supplied names, so a statement of history must say the experiment tested their proposal as well as Kane and Mele's idea. The 3D strand through Fu, Kane and Mele, Moore and Balents, Roy, and Hasan's ARPES is a separate step and is left to a future prize or to nobody. The HgTe edge conductance fell short of perfect quantisation, so a sceptic can call the experimental half thin. The overlap in theme with 2016 is also real, and a critic can call this a second bite at topology. I have not changed my view that these are reasons to write the citation carefully, not reasons to rank B028 below a candidate with its own credit or maturity problems.

responses.point: Danielsson asks what B028 adds beyond the 2016 prize and says that rigorous analysability is not a Nobel criterion; nature has to say something. He prefers a two-part prize of Halzen for IceCube and MacDonald with Jarillo-Herrero for twisted bilayer graphene, and would not oppose B028 if B005 cannot be defended.
responses.response: I agree that analysability is not the criterion, and I accept the challenge. Nature said something specific: a bulk insulator with a spin-orbit gap has conducting edge channels protected by time-reversal symmetry alone, and HgTe wells showed an edge conductance of the order of 2e^2/h, which no one would have asserted without the Z2 argument. That is a different statement from 2016, which did not need spin-orbit coupling, and it did not concern a material class. I also think the two-part route has a cost for me. A three-person ceiling shared across two parts forces you to drop Bistritzer from B046, which you describe as a choice you do not enjoy, and the astrophysical part rests on one name for a collaboration-scale instrument. You say you would not oppose B028 if B005 cannot be defended, and since Pearce, you and Olsson all say the credit for IceCube is unsettled, I would ask you to treat that as a live reason to move here, not only a fallback.

responses.point: Olsson prefers B046 alone with Jarillo-Herrero, MacDonald and Bistritzer, argues that the pairing mechanism need not be settled for a discovery prize, and now says the original experiment and not the earliest related one is the criterion for credit.
responses.response: Your move from Andrei to Bistritzer resolves the weaker credit choice in B046, and I agree with your principle that the criterion is the original experiment. I also accept your point that an unexplained mechanism does not disqualify a discovery, as the cuprates show. Where I still differ is the age of the evidence. The correlated phases have been seen in several moire systems, but a quantitative account of why the superconductivity arises is missing, whereas for B028 band-structure theory reproduces the measured spectra. I applied your principle to B028: the original experiment for the quantum spin Hall effect is Molenkamp's, and I think that is as identifiable as Jarillo-Herrero's. I keep B046 as my first alternative and would not call it a mistake. If the committee finds the two-name credit for B028 unconvincing, I would move to your configuration before I move to a clock prize.

responses.point: Pearce supports B028 with the trio and writes the citation around the quantum spin Hall prediction and first observation; he asks for a form of the distinction from 2016 that can be defended externally, and asks whether the 3D strand should be a second part.
responses.response: I would offer this wording for the external defence: the 2016 prize recognised topological invariants and phase transitions in model systems, and this prize recognises a time-reversal-invariant topological phase in real materials, caused by spin-orbit coupling and not by a magnetic field. On your 3D question, I considered a second part for Hasan and rejected it. A second part would take a fourth seat if we kept three names for the first, or force us to drop one of the three, and the 3D result follows from the same Z2 classification, so it is better described in the background text than as a separate prize. I also appreciate that you put your own B005 as an alternative and not the lead, since I cannot test the detector evidence myself, and I take it that the single-name problem you accept for IceCube is the reason.

responses.point: Eriksson agrees on the trio and the 2016 argument, and in round 1 I said I would hold Hasan as an alternative. He now raises that the 2D and 3D strands test the same Z2 mechanism, and welcomes a citation written narrowly enough not to misstate history.
responses.response: We agree on the substance. Having read the chair's questions, I tried the alternative where Hasan replaces Mele or Molenkamp. It does not work for me. Removing Mele takes out half of the original Z2 theory and removing Molenkamp removes the only experimental half of the 2D story, which Johansson has also argued. A citation that is explicitly about the quantum spin Hall effect and the Z2 phase is then both honest and defensible, with the 3D work and the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal acknowledged in the scientific background. I would now say that my earlier remark that a slate with Hasan is at least as defensible was too generous to the 3D side.

responses.point: Kroll prefers B034 for Katori and Ye, with the cleanest two-name credit on the shortlist and reproduction across Sr, Yb and Hg, and says he could change his mind if someone shows a concrete finding from lattice clocks that nature did not allow us to guess.
responses.response: I take the credit argument seriously, and I do not contest the maturity. My objection is the same one you raise yourself. The gravitational redshift over millimetres, tests of constants and the redefinition of the second are demonstrations of capability or prospects, and the discovery that is already in hand is the magic-wavelength idea and its realisation at the 10^-18 level. That is real and original, but it follows the 2005 and 2012 prizes closely, and Lemonde, Takamoto, Ludlow and Bloom have partial claims you acknowledge. I did not answer the chair's question for you, and I cannot, since I am not an atomic physicist, but I note that neither you nor Lindroth has named a finding that nature surprised us with. That is why I keep B034 as my second alternative and do not move it up.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts a trio that omits Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang and Hasan, or prefers a narrower or broader citation; I cannot verify priority details beyond what the papers claim.
Whether the overlap in theme with the 2016 prize will be read as a second bite despite the different symmetry class and the use of spin-orbit coupling.
Whether the open pairing mechanism in B046 is a reason to wait, which I regard as a judgement on which the condensed-matter members who rank it first are better placed than me.
Whether Halzen alone can be defended for B005, which I cannot judge from the instrument side.
statement.conflict_note: No change. I have no known collaboration or institutional connection with Kane, Mele, Molenkamp, Hasan, or any other credited person on the shortlist. The only point I note is that Johansson and Olsson are in the Gothenburg physics environment, which is an institutional fact and not a connection to any candidate. I have read Johansson's proposed recusal on B035 and have no objection.
